subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Should the centralized filename decoder be accepted as a media-core/plugin-safe shared utility now, or should this issue be narrowed to smaller parser fixes and channel-specific follow-ups?
rationale: Current main proves the split implementation remains, but choosing the permanent shared boundary affects plugin SDK exposure and channel ownership beyond a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Refresh shared media-core decoder
options.body: Use the open shared-decoder PR as source context, move the decoder into the current media-core/plugin-safe boundary, and require targeted proof for remote media plus Feishu paths.

options.title: Narrow to remote-media parser bugs
options.body: Keep this issue open but split immediate work into smaller parser fixes, leaving multi-channel migration for later maintainer-sponsored work.

options.title: Defer broad utility
options.body: Leave only narrow channel fixes active and explicitly defer the cross-channel multi-encoding utility until maintainers want the API surface.

recommendation.title: Refresh shared media-core decoder
recommendation.body: Use the open shared-decoder PR as source context, move the decoder into the current media-core/plugin-safe boundary, and require targeted proof for remote media plus Feishu paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Feishu filename fixes and related media-boundary review history make this the clearest routing owner from the available evidence.
